blocks.text: Neurons vary in shape, but all have three basic parts: a cell body, dendrites and an axon.

blocks.caption: Parts of a neuron
rows: enlarged region with the nucleus and most organelles; its cytoplasm has Nissl's granules, groups of ribosomes and rough endoplasmic reticulum

membrane-bounded extensions that receive information from other cells, turn it into impulses and carry them towards the cell body; motor and inter-neurons, which receive from many sources at once, have highly branched dendrites
a long extension that carries impulses away from the cell body; a neuron may have one axon or branching axons, and its end, the axon terminal, meets a muscle cell, a gland cell or another neuron

blocks.alt: A neuron: branched dendrites around a cell body with its nucleus, and a long axon covered by Schwann cells ending in branched axon terminals. An arrow leads to an enlarged stretch of myelinated axon showing the axon, the myelin sheath wrapped round it, the nucleus of the Schwann cell and a node of Ranvier between two Schwann cells.
blocks.caption: Figure 15.1: Structure of a model neuron (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 15.1).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Dendrites, Nucleus, Cell body, Axon, Schwann cell, Axon terminals; in the enlargement, Node of Ranvier, Nucleus of Schwann cell, Myelin sheath, Axon.

blocks.text: Neuroglia (glial cells) support neurons: they supply nutrients, remove wastes and provide immunity. Two important glial cells, Schwann cells and oligodendrocytes, wrap round axons to make myelin sheaths of many membrane layers: Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system and oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system.

items: The myelin sheath is an insulating cover that speeds the transmission of impulses along the axon.
Neurons with myelin sheaths are myelinated; those without are non-myelinated.
In the CNS, myelinated axons form the white matter, and non-myelinated dendrites and cell bodies the grey matter. In the PNS, myelinated and non-myelinated axons are bundled into nerves.
The myelin sheath is interrupted every 1 to 2 mm by small gaps, the nodes of Ranvier.

blocks.title: Did you know?
blocks.text: Axons can be very long: those controlling the muscles of your feet are more than a metre long, and in a giraffe axons from the skull to the pelvis are about three metres long.
